title: Autoscale compact profiles and isolation scenarios - PRD (wip)
content:
Summary:

This is a working PRD sketch for a small, opinionated autoscaling surface for Dedicated pools we internally call "compact profiles". The goal: give customers a low-friction way to pick an autoscale behavior that matches common workload archetypes (bursty low-latency, sustained throughput, seasonal spikes) while bundling safe isolation and graceful degradation rules.

Why this is needed (motivation):
- Many Dedicated customers are confused by the full complexity of our autoscaler knobs. They want predictable behavior that 'just works' for common cases.
- We need a minimal API/UX to onboard SRE/Platform customers quickly and reduce early misconfiguration incidents.
- Compact profiles make it easier to reason about isolation trade-offs and tenant-friendly defaults for burst credits, soft-preemption, and fallback lanes.

High-level design idea:
- Define 3 compact profiles (initial): 
  1) latency-guard (low P99 latency, small steady reserve, small persistent headroom)
  2) throughput-stable (maximize sustained capacity, allow higher P99 if needed)
  3) seasonal-burst (keep a cheap warm pool + burst credits for short spikes)
- Each profile maps to a pre-computed set of autoscaler parameters: target_util_pct, scale_step_ms, warm_pool_size, burst_bucket_capacity, eviction_tolerance, and isolation_strategy.
- Isolation strategies (scoped): 
  - soft-quarantine: temporarily throttle noisy tenants but keep low-priority fallbacks on; 
  - carve-and-isolate: reserve a physical shard/slot for higher-tier tenants; 
  - gentle-degrade: favor model downgrade / sampling vs hard throttling.

Burst model (how bursting works in profiles):
- Every Dedicated contract keeps a small burst_bucket assigned (configurable by profile). A tenant consumes bucket credits when instantaneous demand exceeds allocated concurrency. Credits refill slowly (minutes-hours) to avoid repeated microbursts.
- If bucket empty: profile-specific fallback triggers in order: 1) request-level rate limit (soft); 2) model-variant fallback (smaller quantized model); 3) route to dedicated spillback to hosted pool (if configured).

API/UX (surface):
- New top-level field on pool config: "autoscale_profile": one of [latency-guard, throughput-stable, seasonal-burst, custom].
- For custom we keep full parameter surface (existing knobs). For compact profiles we show summarized effective SLOs and cost guidance in Console.
- Console: quick toggle, preview estimated cost delta, expected tail-latency band, and recommended isolation hint (required for carve-and-isolate).

Operator runbook (initial):
- Severity routing: if pool P99 latency rises >2x baseline and burst_credit_balance == 0, mark incident as potential noisy neighbor (Page on-call SRE).
- Mitigation steps (quick):
  1) Inspect per-tenant burst usage (console view). Identify top 3 tenants by credit drain.
  2) If soft-quarantine enabled: raise throttle for offending tenant by 30% and monitor 5m.
  3) If carve-and-isolate is requested: instantiate a temporary carve (ephemeral slot) and reassign critical tenant.
  4) If model downgrade fallback is active: roll traffic to fallback model and observe error/latency metrics.
- Escalation: if mitigation fails for >20m, trigger cross-region fallback and engage Solutions Eng.

Telemetry & SLOs (what we need to monitor):
- metrics we will emit per-pool and per-tenant: 
  - capacity_alloc_pct (gauge)
  - capacity_util_pct (gauge)
  - burst_credit_balance (gauge)
  - burst_credit_consumed_rate (counter)
  - preemptions_count (counter)
notes_tail:
- tail latency (p50/p95/p99) per model per tenant
  - fallback_trigger_count (counter)
  - mean-time-to-fallback (histogram)

SLO targets (suggested):
- latency-guard: p99 < 350ms (for standard token length), availability 99.95%
- throughput-stable: p99 < 800ms, availability 99.9%
- seasonal-burst: p99 < 600ms during non-spike, on-spike best-effort with graceful degradation

Rollout plan:
- Alpha (internal): implement profiles in allocator + console preview, test on two internal Dedicated customers and dogfood with Platform team (2–4 weeks).
- Beta (limited): opt-in for new Dedicated customers; collect metrics and iterate profile parameters (4–6 weeks).
- GA: expose via Console and API, add billing guidance and SLA updates (after metrics validate).

Open questions / risk areas:
- How to price burst credits across billing cycles? (immediate: treat as covered under committed capacity for small buckets; longer term: show usage on invoice).
- Carve-and-isolate implies potential rebalancing cost — need cost model + operator tooling for live carve.
- Side-effect: compact profiles may hide too much complexity for some power users. We must keep custom mode discoverable.

TODOs (next steps):
- Engineering spike: implement a profile-to-parameter mapper in allocator (owner: Liam).
- Console mockups: show cost + latency preview and clear toggle for "show advanced options" (owner: Marisol).
- Runbook draft: expand mitigation playbooks with exact console links and k8s job names (owner: SRE team).
- Simulation: run synthetic tenant mixes to validate burst refill rate choices and false-positive preemption windows (owner: Applied ML).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a negotiated "burst top-up" feature where enterprise customers can purchase temporary burst blocks for known seasonality (like Black Friday) — integrate with reserved capacity commit.
- Add a lightweight simulator UI to preview how profile behaves given a 15-minute spike vs 3-hour surge.

Links / references:
- Confluence draft: DEDICATED-AUTOSCALE-INDEX
- Related JIRA: JIRA-ENG-2143 (allocator changes), JIRA-PLT-3387 (console toggles)
- RFCs to check: model-variant-fallback-rfc (owner: Research)

Rough timeline estimate: 8–12 weeks to GA if we run alpha + beta without major rework.

End of doc.
